objects.description: Type-erased metadata describing a scalar element type. Holds size in bytes and flags indicating whether the type is floating-point, signed integer, or bfloat16. Used by helper functions to format values and type names without templated specialization bloat.

Lightweight timestamp value holding seconds since an unspecified origin. Default constructor initializes t using hwy::platform::Now(). Intended for simple wall-time delta measurement via SecondsSince.

Alias for a 64-bit unsigned tick counter representing platform-specific timer units (e.g., TSC cycles on x86). Unsigned to allow wraparound semantics. Use hwy::platform::InvariantTicksPerSecond() to convert to seconds. Note: this is a type alias with no separate storage semantics.

High-level timer facade around low-level fenced Start/Stop tick capture. Constructor probes CPU support for Stop; After() will fall back to Start() if unsupported. Use Before()/After() to bracket measured code with appropriate fences.

Utility for measuring elapsed ticks between calls. Construct with a Timer reference; Reset() sets the origin to the current fenced timestamp. Elapsed() returns ticks since the last origin and updates the origin for reuse.
Strongly-typed bitflag enum controlling profiler zone behavior (currently supports kInclusive to report inclusive time). Backed by uint32_t for safe casting.
Type-safe handle encoding a profiler zone index and flags within a compact 32-bit field. Used to identify zones and check inclusive behavior.
Primary profiler singleton managing per-worker state, zone registry, accumulation, callbacks, and reporting. Provides thread index management and zone entry/exit API.
RAII helper that records a zone’s begin/end timestamps and notifies Profiler for the given worker and zone handle. Construct on scope entry to time that scope.
Stub empty ZoneHandle definition used when PROFILER_ENABLED == 0. Carries no data; acts only to satisfy interfaces.
Stub Profiler definition when profiling is disabled. Provides no-op methods and static Get() declaration for link compatibility.
Stub Zone with no timing behavior, compiled when profiling is disabled.
Internal tuning parameters for the nanobenchmark measurement procedure, determining precision, sample sizes, stopping criteria, and verbosity. Fields are initialized with reasonable defaults.
Per-input measurement summary returned by Measure/MeasureClosure, including the input value, estimated duration in timer ticks, and relative variability.

objects.definition: using FuncInput = size_t;
objects.description: Alias for the input type passed to the function under test; represents the varying argument (e.g., byte count).

objects.definition: using FuncOutput = uint64_t;
objects.description: Alias for the return type of the function under test; acts as a proof-of-work to prevent elision by the compiler.

objects.definition: using Func = FuncOutput (*)(const void*, FuncInput);
objects.description: Function pointer type for measured functions. The first const void* parameter is either a user argument or an internal pointer to a closure; the second is the varying input. Returns a proof-of-work value.
Custom deleter for aligned objects/arrays that explicitly invokes element destructors and then frees memory via provided FreePtr/opaque context.
Custom deleter for aligned memory that simply frees the memory using FreeAlignedBytes; intended for trivially destructible types (POD).

Thread-safe (except when HWY_NO_LIBCXX is defined) small state object storing a bitmask representing the currently chosen/eligible SIMD targets for dynamic dispatch within Highway. Provides methods to update/reset initialization state and to compute the dispatch table index for the active target set.
This header defines no custom types. It is an empty compatibility header; all Abort/Warn functionality lives elsewhere (base.h). No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are introduced here.

functions.name: hwy::DeduceFunctionCache
functions.signature:
template <typename RetType, typename... Args>
FunctionCache<RetType, Args...> hwy::DeduceFunctionCache(RetType (*)(Args...));
functions.description: Helper template function that deduces the return type and parameter types from a function pointer and returns the corresponding FunctionCache<RetType, Args...> type. Used internally to obtain the correct FunctionCache specialization for building and invoking dispatch tables. Typical usage is passing a function pointer (e.g., &HWY_STATIC_DISPATCH(FUNC_NAME)) so that its type can be used in compile-time expressions/macros.
requirements: Argument must be a function pointer of type RetType (*)(Args...).
The function pointer must not be an ambiguous overload; ensure the pointer refers to a specific function signature.
Intended for type deduction; the returned FunctionCache object is a lightweight value used in compile-time context.

functions.name: hwy::FNV
functions.signature: static constexpr uint64_t hwy::FNV(const char* name);
functions.description: Computes a 64-bit FNV-1a-like hash of a null-terminated C string. Used to hash dispatch table names for mapping functions to tables when building dynamic dispatch structures. constexpr enables compile-time evaluation when given a compile-time string.
requirements: Input must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
The function is available only when HWY_DISPATCH_MAP is enabled in this build configuration.
For compile-time evaluation, pass a string literal or otherwise constant expression; otherwise it may be evaluated at runtime.

functions.name: hwy::detail::TypeName
functions.signature: HWY_DLLEXPORT void hwy::detail::TypeName(const hwy::detail::TypeInfo& info, size_t N, char* string100);
functions.description: Formats a human-readable name for the type described by info, potentially including vector length N, and writes it into the provided output buffer string100. Intended for internal printing/utilities to reduce template bloat.
requirements: info must describe a valid C++ type (e.g., produced by hwy::detail::MakeTypeInfo<T>())
string100 must be a non-null pointer to a writable character buffer with capacity for at least 100 bytes (including the terminating null)
The contents of string100 are overwritten; caller should not assume prior contents are preserved
N is used for formatting; valid ranges are unknown, but it should be a sensible non-negative size_t

functions.name: hwy::detail::ToString
functions.signature: HWY_DLLEXPORT void hwy::detail::ToString(const hwy::detail::TypeInfo& info, const void* ptr, char* string100);
functions.description: Converts the value pointed to by ptr, interpreted as the type described by info, into a textual representation and writes it into string100. Used by higher-level helpers to print single values in a type-erased manner.
requirements: info must correspond to the actual dynamic type of the object pointed to by ptr (e.g., constructed via hwy::detail::MakeTypeInfo<T>() for the same T as *ptr)
ptr must be non-null and point to a valid, fully initialized object of the type described by info
string100 must be a non-null pointer to a writable character buffer with capacity for at least 100 bytes (including the terminating null)
The function writes a null-terminated C string into string100; previous contents are overwritten

functions.name: hwy::detail::PrintArray
functions.signature: HWY_DLLEXPORT void hwy::detail::PrintArray(const hwy::detail::TypeInfo& info, const char* caption, const void* array_void, size_t N, size_t lane_u = 0, size_t max_lanes = 7);
functions.description: Prints up to max_lanes elements from an array of N values whose element type is described by info. The output may include the optional caption and may highlight or offset by lane_u. Intended for internal/debug printing of vector lanes or arrays using type-erased element access.
requirements: info must describe the element type of the array (e.g., produced by hwy::detail::MakeTypeInfo<T>() for the same T as the array elements)
caption should be a valid null-terminated C string pointer (may be an empty string)
array_void must be non-null if N > 0 and must point to an array of at least N elements of the type described by info
N is the number of elements available at array_void; it should not exceed the actual array length
If provided, lane_u should be within the range [0, N) to avoid out-of-bounds access or undefined behavior (exact semantics unknown)
max_lanes should be a positive value; behavior for 0 is unknown
Output destination/format is not specified here (likely standard error); callers should not rely on a particular stream or format without checking implementation

functions.name: hwy::PrintValue
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
HWY_NOINLINE void hwy::PrintValue(T value);
functions.description: Formats value of type T to a string and writes it to the process’s error stream followed by a comma. This thin wrapper constructs type information for T and delegates formatting to hwy::detail::ToString.
requirements: T must be supported by hwy::detail::MakeTypeInfo<T>() and hwy::detail::ToString (i.e., ToString must understand the type)
The function writes to stderr via fprintf; callers should ensure this is acceptable in their environment
Value is passed by value; if T is large or non-trivially copyable, consider costs
Thread-safety of concurrent printing is unspecified; interleaving with other output may occur

functions.name: hwy::PrintArray
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
HWY_NOINLINE void hwy::PrintArray(const T* value, size_t count);
functions.description: Prints count elements from the array value using type-erased formatting, delegating to hwy::detail::PrintArray with an empty caption. Intended for debugging or inspecting arrays/vectors of T.
requirements: value must be non-null if count > 0 and must point to an array of at least count elements of type T
count specifies the number of elements to print; it should not exceed the actual array length
T must be supported by hwy::detail::MakeTypeInfo<T>() and hwy::detail::PrintArray
The function likely writes to stderr; output ordering with other threads is unspecified

functions.name: hwy::platform::Now
functions.description: Returns the current monotonic, steady, high-resolution timestamp in seconds relative to an unspecified origin. Intended for measuring elapsed wall-clock time independent of system time changes.

functions.name: hwy::platform::HaveTimerStop
functions.description: Reports whether it is safe to call hwy::timer::Stop on the current CPU without triggering an illegal instruction. If it returns false, it fills the provided buffer with a descriptive CPU string via GetCpuString.
requirements: cpu100 must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least 100 bytes to hold a NUL-terminated string.
Callers should check the return value; if false, do not call hwy::timer::Stop on x86.
On success (true), the buffer may be left unused.

functions.name: hwy::platform::InvariantTicksPerSecond
functions.description: Returns the frequency (ticks per second) of the underlying invariant tick counter, suitable for converting hwy::timer::Ticks to seconds. The rate is intended to be independent of CPU throttling or sleep.
requirements: This call may be expensive; callers should cache the returned value for reuse.

functions.name: hwy::platform::TimerResolution
functions.description: Estimates the timer’s resolution/overhead by returning the ticks elapsed between back-to-back timer calls. Useful for understanding minimum measurable intervals.
requirements: This call is expensive; callers should cache the returned value for reuse.

functions.name: hwy::platform::GetCpuString
functions.description: Fills up to 100 characters (including the terminating NUL) with a human-readable CPU model/identifier string if available. Returns false if a detailed description is not available.
requirements: cpu100 must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer of at least 100 bytes.
Callers should check the return value; if false, the buffer may not contain a detailed CPU description.

functions.name: hwy::SecondsSince
functions.description: Returns the elapsed seconds since the provided Timestamp, computed as Now() - t0. Intended for simple wall-clock interval measurement using hwy::Timestamp.
requirements: t0 must be a valid hwy::Timestamp initialized from the same clock (constructed via its default constructor or otherwise holding a value from hwy::platform::Now).

functions.name: hwy::timer::Start
functions.description: Returns an absolute timestamp in platform-specific ticks, placing fences to prevent instructions from the surrounding code from leaking into the measured region. Use immediately before the code region to measure and pair with hwy::timer::Stop (preferred) or another Start to compute elapsed ticks by subtraction.
requirements: Must be called immediately before the region to measure to ensure accurate fencing.
Returned value is an absolute tick count; compute elapsed time as (end - start).
Ticks may wrap around; subtraction of unsigned ticks handles wraparound semantics.

functions.name: hwy::timer::Stop
functions.description: Returns an absolute timestamp in platform-specific ticks using RDTSCP+LFENCE (or platform equivalents) to prevent subsequent instructions from leaking into the measured region. Intended to be called immediately after the measured region and paired with hwy::timer::Start.
requirements: On x86, callers must first check hwy::platform::HaveTimerStop and only call Stop if it returns true; otherwise calling Stop may execute an illegal instruction.
Must be called immediately after the region to measure to ensure accurate fencing.
Returned value is an absolute tick count; compute elapsed time as (end - start).

functions.name: hwy::Timer::Before
functions.description: Wrapper around hwy::timer::Start that provides the pre-region timestamp with appropriate fences. Use Immediately before the code under test when using hwy::Timer.
requirements: Call immediately before the measured region.
A hwy::Timer instance must have been constructed; it internally determines Stop availability.

functions.name: hwy::Timer::After
functions.description: Wrapper that returns the post-region timestamp. Uses hwy::timer::Stop when supported by the CPU; otherwise falls back to hwy::timer::Start, ensuring safe usage on platforms where Stop is unavailable.
requirements: Call immediately after the measured region.
Relies on the hwy::Timer instance having been constructed so that Stop support was probed.

functions.name: hwy::Seconds
functions.description: Converts platform-specific ticks to seconds using hwy::platform::InvariantTicksPerSecond. Useful for obtaining wall-clock seconds from Start/Stop tick differences.
requirements: Callers should ensure the tick values originate from the same clock/frequency as returned by InvariantTicksPerSecond.

functions.name: hwy::Stopwatch::Origin
functions.description: Returns the current start tick (origin) of the Stopwatch. Useful for diagnostics or custom elapsed computations.
requirements: The hwy::Stopwatch must have been constructed with a valid hwy::Timer reference that outlives the Stopwatch object.

functions.name: hwy::Stopwatch::Reset
functions.description: Resets the Stopwatch’s origin to the current pre-region timestamp by calling timer.Before(). Use to start a new measurement interval.
requirements: The hwy::Stopwatch must have been constructed with a valid hwy::Timer reference that outlives the Stopwatch object.

functions.name: hwy::Stopwatch::Elapsed
functions.description: Returns the ticks elapsed since the last origin and resets the origin to the current post-region timestamp, enabling repeated interval measurements with a single Stopwatch instance.
requirements: Call only on a hwy::Stopwatch constructed with a valid hwy::Timer reference that outlives the Stopwatch object.
Must be paired with the same clock source as provided by the Timer; the method assumes Before/After use the same tick source.

functions.name: hwy::DispatchedTarget
functions.description: Returns the HWY_TARGET value that HWY_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH selected for the current call site. Use this to inspect which target was chosen at runtime. Details of the HWY_TARGET encoding are not documented here and are unknown from this header.
requirements: No arguments required.
Intended as a query; may be called at any time to obtain the dispatched target.
Return value encoding of HWY_TARGET is unspecified in this header; callers must not assume a particular encoding without consulting Highway docs.

functions.name: hwy::VectorBytes
functions.description: Returns the current vector size in bytes (equivalent to Lanes(ScalableTag<uint8_t>())). This can change at runtime (e.g., after DisableTargets or when entering/exiting SME streaming mode). The call involves an indirect call; avoid calling it more often than necessary.
requirements: Do not cache the result across calls that might change the vector size (e.g., after calling DisableTargets or across SME streaming mode transitions).
Call this immediately before code that depends on the vector size, with no intervening DisableTargets calls or SME transitions.
Avoid calling frequently or unnecessarily due to the indirect call overhead.

functions.name: hwy::HaveInteger64
functions.description: Returns whether 64-bit integer lanes are supported for the currently dispatched target. Intended as a capability query before using 64-bit integer operations with Highway.
requirements: No arguments required.
Intended as a pure capability query; can be called at any time to check support.

functions.name: hwy::HaveFloat16
functions.description: Returns whether 16-bit floating-point lanes are supported for the currently dispatched target. Intended as a capability query before using float16 lanes with Highway.
requirements: No arguments required.
Intended as a pure capability query; can be called at any time to check support.

functions.name: hwy::HaveFloat64
functions.description: Returns whether 64-bit floating-point lanes are supported for the currently dispatched target. Intended as a capability query before using double-precision lanes with Highway.
requirements: No arguments required.
Intended as a pure capability query; can be called at any time to check support.

functions.name: hwy::StringTable<kMaxStrings>::Name
functions.description: Returns the interned string pointer previously stored at the given index. Intended to retrieve a name that was earlier inserted via Add and whose index was returned to the caller. Thread-safe for concurrent readers.
requirements: idx must be less than the table capacity kMaxStrings (0 < idx < kMaxStrings).
The index must refer to a string previously added via Add; otherwise behavior is undefined (internal asserts assume a valid, previously published entry).
The returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the StringTable instance.

functions.name: hwy::StringTable<kMaxStrings>::Add
functions.description: Adds (interns) a NUL-terminated string into the table if not already present and returns its stable index. If the same name is added multiple times, all calls return the same index. Safe for concurrent calls from multiple threads.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
The number of unique strings added must be less than kMaxStrings.

Average string length must be short enough that the internal character buffer (kMaxStrings * 55 bytes) is not exhausted; extremely long or too many unique names can overflow in debug builds (asserts).
May be called concurrently by multiple threads; identical names from different threads are deduplicated.

functions.name: hwy::profiler::Zones::Name
functions.description: Returns the zone name previously registered via AddZone for the given ZoneHandle. Wrapper around the underlying StringTable.
requirements: zone must be a valid ZoneHandle previously returned by AddZone.
The ZoneHandle must have a non-zero index within the supported range (< kMaxZones).

functions.name: hwy::profiler::Zones::AddZone
functions.signature: hwy::profiler::ZoneHandle hwy::profiler::Zones::AddZone(const char* name, hwy::ProfilerFlags flags)
functions.description: Registers a zone name with optional flags and returns a type-safe ZoneHandle encoding the zone index and flags. Multiple calls with the same name return equivalent handles (same index). Safe to call concurrently.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
The total number of unique zone names must be less than kMaxZones.
flags must be a valid ProfilerFlags value (currently kDefault or kInclusive).

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::Get
functions.description: Returns the process-wide Profiler singleton. Use this to register zones and control profiling (IsRootRun/EndRootRun/PrintResults).
requirements: Must be called before using other non-static Profiler APIs.
Thread-safe to obtain the reference; subsequent usage must respect each API’s threading requirements.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::Thread
functions.description: Deprecated alias for GlobalIdx. Returns the calling thread’s global worker index (0 for main thread).
requirements: Deprecated: prefer GlobalIdx. Returns 0 if not explicitly set via SetGlobalIdx in disabled build or main thread in enabled build.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::GlobalIdx
functions.description: Returns the calling thread’s global worker index (0 for main thread). Used by legacy PROFILER_ZONE/PROFILER_FUNC macros when a global index is not explicitly passed.
requirements: Must have been previously set via SetGlobalIdx on each worker thread and once on the main thread before using macros that rely on it when the profiler is enabled.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::SetGlobalIdx
functions.description: Sets the calling thread’s global worker index to be used by profiling zones that don’t explicitly pass an index.
requirements: Must be called on all worker threads and once on the main thread before using PROFILER_ZONE/PROFILER_FUNC when relying on implicit index.
global_idx should be less than the maximum supported workers (kMaxWorkers) and unique per concurrently active worker thread.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::ReserveWorker
functions.description: Marks a worker index as reserved/active for profiling. Used by thread pool integrations to announce a worker’s participation so its data can be collected.
requirements: global_idx must be less than kMaxWorkers.
Must not be called for an index that is already reserved (debug assertions enforce).
Each reserved index should later be released via FreeWorker(global_idx).
Should be called before entering any zones with that global_idx.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::FreeWorker
functions.description: Marks a previously reserved worker index as free/inactive, stopping further result collection for that worker.
requirements: global_idx must be less than kMaxWorkers.
Must be called only for an index that is currently reserved (debug assertions enforce).
Should be paired with a prior ReserveWorker(global_idx) call.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::Enter
functions.description: Notifies the profiler that a zone has been entered at time t_enter for the specified worker. Typically called by the profiler::Zone RAII object, not directly by users.
requirements: global_idx must correspond to a currently reserved worker index.
t_enter must be a timestamp obtained from the profiler’s timer (timer::Start).
May be called from any thread as long as calls for a given global_idx are not concurrent.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::Exit
functions.signature: void hwy::Profiler::Exit(uint64_t t_exit, size_t global_idx, hwy::profiler::ZoneHandle zone)
functions.description: Notifies the profiler that a zone has been exited at time t_exit for the specified worker and zone. Computes and accumulates self time (or inclusive time if flagged). Typically called by the profiler::Zone destructor.
requirements: global_idx must correspond to a currently reserved worker index.
zone must be a valid ZoneHandle for the zone being exited.
t_exit must be a timestamp obtained from the profiler’s timer (timer::Stop).
Enter/Exit calls for the same global_idx must be properly nested; no concurrent usage with the same global_idx.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::GetFirstDurationAndReset
functions.description: Returns the measured duration of the first recorded enter/exit pair for the given worker and resets associated state. Used internally for overhead detection/initialization.
requirements: global_idx must correspond to a reserved worker index with exactly one zone recorded as per the internal expectations (used during self-overhead detection).
Intended for internal use; callers should avoid using this unless implementing profiler internals.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::Name
functions.description: Returns the zone name associated with the given ZoneHandle. Convenience wrapper around internal storage.
requirements: zone must be a valid ZoneHandle previously returned by AddZone.
Returned pointer remains valid while the profiler is alive.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::AddZone
functions.signature: hwy::profiler::ZoneHandle hwy::Profiler::AddZone(const char* name, hwy::ProfilerFlags flags = hwy::ProfilerFlags::kDefault)
functions.description: Registers a zone name with optional flags and returns a ZoneHandle to use when creating profiler::Zone scopes. Can be invoked during static initialization and is safe across threads.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string.
The total number of unique zones must be less than kMaxZones.
flags must be a valid ProfilerFlags value (kDefault or kInclusive).

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::AddFunc
functions.description: Registers a callback function to be invoked during PrintResults. Used by other modules (e.g., thread pools) to contribute additional data. Thread-safe.
requirements: owner must be a non-null unique key pointer identifying the registrant.
func must be a valid callable (non-empty).
Each owner should register at most one function at a time; duplicate keys are not allowed.
Must later call RemoveFunc with the same owner to unregister.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::RemoveFunc
functions.description: Unregisters a previously added callback identified by owner. Thread-safe.
requirements: owner must be the same non-null key used in a prior AddFunc call.
There must have been a prior AddFunc for this owner; removing a non-existent key is an error (internal abort).
Expected usage is to remove exactly once, typically from the same thread that added it (per internal comment).

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::IsRootRun
functions.description: Indicates whether a new root ThreadPool::Run section is starting. Returns true exactly for the first call that marks a root run since the last EndRootRun, and false while a run is active. Used to gate EndRootRun calls and aggregate concurrency statistics.
requirements: Should be called on the main thread that orchestrates runs.
If this returns true, the caller must later invoke EndRootRun().
Not reentrant; concurrent root runs are not supported.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::EndRootRun
functions.description: Ends a root run previously acknowledged by IsRootRun(), moves per-worker accumulators into global results, updates concurrency stats, and allows the next IsRootRun() to return true.
requirements: Must be called only if a preceding IsRootRun() call returned true.
Should be called from the main thread.
Some zones may still be active; the function accounts for that when results are later printed.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::PrintResults
functions.description: Aggregates remaining per-worker data, prints sorted zone statistics to stdout, resets internal totals, and invokes any registered callbacks via AddFunc. Intended to be called after all threads have exited zones.
requirements: Should be called from the main thread after all threads have exited all zones to ensure final, consistent results.
Safe to call multiple times; internal state is reset between calls.
If concurrency is tracked via IsRootRun/EndRootRun, those should bracket runs appropriately for meaningful concurrency figures.

functions.name: hwy::Profiler::SetMaxThreads
functions.description: Deprecated/no-op placeholder retained for compatibility. Does not affect behavior.
requirements: No specific requirements; parameter is ignored.

functions.name: hwy::profiler::Zone::Zone
functions.signature: hwy::profiler::Zone::Zone(hwy::Profiler& profiler, size_t global_idx, hwy::profiler::ZoneHandle zone)
functions.description: RAII scope object that records entry time on construction and exit time on destruction, attributing time to the given zone and worker. Creates a profiling region spanning the Zone object’s lifetime.
requirements: profiler must be a valid Profiler instance (typically hwy::Profiler::Get()).
global_idx must be the caller’s global worker index; calls for the same global_idx must not overlap/concurrently execute.
zone must be a valid ZoneHandle previously obtained from Profiler::AddZone.
Construction/destruction should occur on the same thread; rely on the timer functions to obtain t_enter/t_exit.

functions.name: hwy::profiler::Zone::~Zone
functions.description: Destructor that closes the profiling scope started by the constructor, records the exit timestamp, and submits accumulated time to the profiler.
requirements: Must correspond to a previously constructed Zone object; should run on the same thread as the constructor to preserve nesting correctness.
No explicit caller action required; triggered automatically at end of scope.

functions.name: hwy::Unpredictable1
functions.description: Returns the integer value 1 in a way that prevents the compiler from predicting or optimizing around the value. Useful for inhibiting constant-folding and branch prediction during benchmarks or tests.
requirements: No arguments required.
May be called at any time; has no side effects and no preconditions.
Return value is always 1; callers can use it in expressions to prevent compile-time optimization.

functions.name: hwy::Measure
functions.signature: HWY_DLLEXPORT size_t hwy::Measure(hwy::Func func, const uint8_t* arg, const hwy::FuncInput* inputs, size_t num_inputs, hwy::Result* results, const hwy::Params& p = hwy::Params());
functions.description: Measures, with high precision, the elapsed timer ticks for calling a function (Func) across a distribution of inputs, shuffled to yield realistic branch prediction hit rates. Writes one Result per unique input value and returns the number of results written, or 0 on failure (an error message is printed to stderr). Intended for microbenchmarking functions that take (const void*, FuncInput) and return a 64-bit proof-of-work value.
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer matching FuncOutput (*)(const void*, FuncInput).
arg is passed as the first parameter to func (or reserved internally when using MeasureClosure). If func expects to use it, arg must point to valid memory for the duration of the call(s).
inputs must point to an array of length num_inputs. The array may contain duplicates to represent a distribution; order does not matter.
num_inputs can be zero or more. If zero, behavior/result count is implementation-defined; typically no measurements will be produced.
results must point to writable storage large enough for at least the number of unique values present in inputs; one Result is written per unique input value.
The return value is the number of Result entries written; callers should check for 0 to detect failure (error details are sent to stderr).
When providing a custom Params p: p.subset_ratio must be >= 2 (per documentation). Other fields influence precision and runtime but impose no additional functional constraints.
func should be safe to call repeatedly and reentrantly across the provided input distribution, and must not rely on global state that would make repeated calls invalid or unsafe.
func must tolerate every value present in inputs; passing values outside func’s supported domain is a caller error.

functions.name: hwy::MeasureClosure
functions.signature:
template <class Closure>
static inline size_t hwy::MeasureClosure(const Closure& closure, const hwy::FuncInput* inputs, const size_t num_inputs, hwy::Result* results, const hwy::Params& p = hwy::Params());
functions.description: Convenience wrapper around Measure for callable objects (typically lambdas with captures) whose operator() has signature FuncOutput(FuncInput). Internally forwards to Measure by passing a trampoline (CallClosure) and the address of the closure object. Returns the number of Result entries written (one per unique input), or 0 on failure (error to stderr).
requirements: Closure must be callable as FuncOutput operator()(FuncInput) const (compatible with being invoked via a const pointer).
closure must remain valid for the duration of the call; it is passed by const reference and its address is used internally during measurement.
inputs must point to an array of length num_inputs; may contain duplicates to represent a distribution; order does not matter.
results must point to writable storage sufficient for at least the number of unique values in inputs.
Callers should check the return value; 0 indicates failure (error details printed to stderr).
When providing a custom Params p: p.subset_ratio must be >= 2 (per documentation). Other fields only affect precision/runtime.
The closure’s operator() should be safe to call repeatedly and reentrantly for all provided input values and must not have side effects that make repeated measurements invalid.
The closure must accept and correctly handle every value present in inputs; providing unsupported values is a caller error.

functions.name: hwy::IsAligned
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
constexpr bool hwy::IsAligned(T* ptr, size_t align = HWY_ALIGNMENT)
functions.description: Checks whether ptr is aligned to the specified byte boundary (default HWY_ALIGNMENT, 128). Returns true if the pointer address modulo align is zero. Useful before using SIMD assumptions that require literal alignment.
requirements: ptr may be null; the function will still compute alignment on the address value.

functions.name: hwy::SupportedTargets
functions.description: Returns a bitfield mask of enabled SIMD targets supported on the current CPU. The value is never 0; if all targets would otherwise be disabled, a fallback target (e.g., HWY_STATIC_TARGET) is returned. The set may change after calls to DisableTargets or SetSupportedTargetsForTest. Always defined; callers may use the HWY_SUPPORTED_TARGETS macro to elide the call when only a single target is enabled.
requirements: No arguments required.
Return is a non-zero 64-bit bitmask composed of HWY_* target bits.
The returned mask may change across calls if DisableTargets or SetSupportedTargetsForTest have been used.
No explicit thread-safety guarantees are documented for calling this function; treat as unknown.

functions.name: hwy::DisableTargets
functions.description: Globally disables a set of targets so that subsequent SupportedTargets() calls will not include those targets. Useful to avoid buggy or undesirable targets. If disabling all would make SupportedTargets return 0, a fallback target will be returned instead to ensure there is always at least one callable target.
requirements: disabled_targets is a bitmask of HWY_* target bits to disable.
Affects global target selection used by SupportedTargets().
For testing multiple specific targets iteratively, prefer SetSupportedTargetsForTest instead (per documentation).
Thread-safety and lifetime effects are not documented; treat as unknown.

functions.name: hwy::SetSupportedTargetsForTest
functions.description: Overrides the set of targets returned by SupportedTargets() with the provided bitmask (still honoring any targets disabled via DisableTargets). Calling with 0 disables the override and restores normal SupportedTargets behavior. Intended for testing across all targets.
requirements: targets is a bitmask of HWY_* target bits representing the desired mock set.
Passing targets == 0 disables the mock and restores normal behavior.
This setting influences subsequent SupportedTargets() calls only; it does not re-enable targets disabled by DisableTargets.
Thread-safety and scope of the override across threads/DSOs are not documented; treat as unknown.

functions.name: hwy::TargetName
functions.signature: static inline HWY_MAYBE_UNUSED const char* hwy::TargetName(int64_t target);
functions.description: Returns a stable C string name for a single HWY_* target value (e.g., "SSE2", "AVX2", "NEON"). Intended to produce a gtest IsValidParamName() compatible string. If the value is not recognized, returns "Unknown".
requirements: target should be a single HWY_* target macro value (one-bit mask corresponding to a specific target).
If target is not one of the recognized HWY_* values for any architecture, the function returns "Unknown".
The returned pointer is to a static string literal and remains valid for the lifetime of the program.

functions.name: hwy::GetChosenTarget
functions.description: Returns a reference to the process-wide ChosenTarget singleton used internally by Highway (e.g., by FunctionCache and DisableTargets) to manage dynamic dispatch state. The returned reference can be used to inspect/update target selection via ChosenTarget’s methods.
requirements: Do not attempt to delete or free the returned reference; it refers to internal static storage.
On architectures where ChosenTarget is not thread-safe (comment notes: thread-safe except on RVV), callers must avoid data races when using the returned object.
The validity of the reference is for the lifetime of the process; module/DSO boundary behaviors are not documented.

functions.name: hwy::LoadFence
functions.description: Issues a load fence that delays subsequent loads until prior loads become visible. On some architectures (notably Intel x86) it can behave as a full fence. Intended for fine-grained memory-ordering control when coordinating dependent loads.
requirements: May be a no-op on platforms where cache-control is disabled (HWY_DISABLE_CACHE_CONTROL).
Use only when a load-ordering barrier is required; it does not perform synchronization beyond ordering loads.

functions.name: hwy::StreamCacheLine
functions.signature: void StreamCacheLine(const uint64_t* from, uint64_t* to);
functions.description: Streams one cache line worth of data from 'from' to 'to', attempting to bypass the cache (read-for-ownership) when available. Falls back to a regular byte copy if non-temporal stores are unavailable. Intended for writing out a cache line without polluting caches.
requirements: Both 'from' and 'to' must be aligned (intended to HWY_ALIGNMENT).
Both pointers must be valid for at least HWY_ALIGNMENT bytes starting at the given addresses.
The function overwrites the destination range unconditionally.

functions.name: hwy::FlushStream
functions.description: Ensures that values written by previous streaming (non-temporal) stores are made visible on the current core. Acts as a store fence on supported architectures.
requirements: Call after issuing prior streaming writes whose visibility must be ensured on the current core.
This is not sufficient for inter-core synchronization; if other cores will consume the data, publish availability via proper synchronization (e.g., mutex or atomic) after calling FlushStream.
May be a no-op on platforms where cache-control is disabled.

functions.name: hwy::Prefetch
functions.signature: template <typename T> void Prefetch(const T* p);
functions.description: Hints the CPU to begin loading the cache line containing address 'p' to reduce latency of subsequent actual loads. Uses platform intrinsics when available; otherwise may be a no-op.
requirements: Pointer 'p' is not dereferenced by this function; no alignment requirement is specified.
Effect is advisory and platform-dependent; may be a no-op when cache-control is disabled.

functions.name: hwy::FlushCacheline
functions.description: Invalidates and flushes the cache line containing address 'p', if supported by the architecture. On unsupported platforms it does nothing.
requirements: Address 'p' designates the memory whose cache line you intend to flush; no alignment requirement is specified.
May be a no-op on non-x86 or when cache-control is disabled.

functions.name: hwy::Pause
functions.description: Issues a processor hint that the calling thread is in a spin loop, potentially reducing power and coherency traffic and improving forward progress. Uses the best available instruction per architecture; otherwise may be a no-op.
requirements: Call inside busy-wait/spin loops to reduce contention; outside of such loops it provides no benefit.
May be a no-op on platforms where the hint is unavailable or cache-control is disabled.

functions.name: hwy::robust_statistics::CountingSort
functions.signature:
template <class T>
void hwy::robust_statistics::CountingSort(T* values, size_t num_values)
functions.description: In-place stable-like counting-style sort for integral-like data. Sorts the input values array in ascending order, optimized for inputs with few unique values. Intended for preparing data for mode estimation, but usable as a general in-place sort when T supports ordering.
requirements: values must point to an array of at least num_values elements
values may be null only if num_values == 0
Sorting is in-place and will mutate the contents of values
T must be equality comparable (operator==) and totally ordered (operator<) to support std::pair<T,int> sorting
T must be copy-assignable/movable (used by std::vector and std::fill)
num_values may be zero; the function is a no-op in that case

functions.name: hwy::robust_statistics::MinRange
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
size_t hwy::robust_statistics::MinRange(const T* const HWY_RESTRICT sorted, const size_t idx_begin, const size_t half_count)
functions.description: Finds the start index i in [idx_begin, idx_begin + half_count) that minimizes the window width sorted[i + half_count] - sorted[i] in a sorted array. Used as a step of the Half Sample Mode estimator.
requirements: sorted must reference a sequence in nondecreasing (ascending) order
half_count must be > 0 to obtain a meaningful result; if half_count == 0, the loop does not run and the return value is 0
The valid index range must cover accesses up to sorted[idx_begin + 2*half_count - 1]
T must support subtraction (operator-) and comparison (operator<) and be compatible with std::numeric_limits<T>::max()
sorted must not be null for half_count > 0

functions.name: hwy::robust_statistics::ModeOfSorted
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T hwy::robust_statistics::ModeOfSorted(const T* const HWY_RESTRICT sorted, const size_t num_values)
functions.description: Computes a robust estimate of the mode from a sorted array using the Half Sample Mode (Bickel) by repeatedly selecting the narrowest half-interval. For the final two-point case it returns the rounded average of the two values, assuming an unsigned integer T.
requirements: sorted must point to at least num_values elements
num_values must be > 0
sorted must be in nondecreasing (ascending) order
For the final averaging step, T is assumed to be an unsigned integer type; using signed or non-integer types changes rounding semantics
T must support indexing, addition, division by 2, subtraction, and comparisons as used by MinRange
sorted must not be null when num_values > 0

functions.name: hwy::robust_statistics::Mode
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T hwy::robust_statistics::Mode(T* values, const size_t num_values)
functions.description: Returns the mode estimate of the input by first sorting values in place (CountingSort) and then applying the Half Sample Mode on the sorted data. Intended for unsigned integer types.
requirements: values must point to at least num_values elements
num_values must be > 0
values will be sorted in ascending order as a side effect
T should be an unsigned integer type for the estimator’s final averaging semantics
values must not be null when num_values > 0

functions.name: hwy::robust_statistics::Median
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T hwy::robust_statistics::Median(T* values, const size_t num_values)
functions.description: Computes the median in place by sorting the array. For odd counts, returns the middle element. For even counts, returns the rounded average of the two middle elements when T is an integer type, otherwise the arithmetic mean.
requirements: num_values must be != 0
values must point to at least num_values elements
values will be sorted in ascending order as a side effect
T must be totally ordered (operator<) for std::sort
For even counts, T must support addition and division by 2; rounding-to-nearest is applied for integer T via a +1 bias

functions.name: hwy::robust_statistics::MedianAbsoluteDeviation
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T hwy::robust_statistics::MedianAbsoluteDeviation(const T* values, const size_t num_values, const T median)
functions.description: Computes the Median Absolute Deviation (MAD), a robust measure of variability, as the median of |values[i] − median|. Deviations are computed via int64_t arithmetic and cast back to T before taking the median.
requirements: num_values must be != 0
values must point to at least num_values elements and must not be null when num_values > 0
median should be the median of the same sample (typically from hwy::robust_statistics::Median)
T must be convertible to and from int64_t without undefined behavior for the value range used (deviations are computed in int64_t)
T must be supported by Median(T*, size_t) (i.e., sortable, add/divide as required there)

functions.name: hwy::x86::Cpuid
functions.signature: static inline void hwy::x86::Cpuid(const uint32_t level, const uint32_t count, uint32_t* HWY_RESTRICT abcd)
functions.description: Executes the x86 CPUID instruction for the specified leaf (level) and subleaf (count) and writes the results into abcd as {EAX, EBX, ECX, EDX}. Intended for querying CPU feature bits and vendor/feature information. Use when you need raw CPUID values for a given leaf/subleaf; the caller interprets the returned registers.
requirements: Must be compiled and run on an x86/x86_64 target (guarded by HWY_ARCH_X86).
abcd must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for at least 4 uint32_t elements.

If the requested CPUID leaf/subleaf is not supported by the CPU, returned values are CPU-defined; callers expecting specific bits must ensure the leaf is supported (e.g., by checking MaxLevel or equivalent mechanisms).

functions.name: hwy::x86::IsBitSet
functions.signature: static inline bool hwy::x86::IsBitSet(const uint32_t reg, const int index)
functions.description: Tests whether the bit at position index is set in reg. Useful for checking individual CPUID feature bits or any 32-bit flag field.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, 31]; shifting by >=32 is undefined behavior in C/C++.
reg may be any 32-bit value.

functions.name: hwy::x86::MaxLevel
functions.description: Returns the maximum supported CPUID basic leaf by executing CPUID with EAX=0 and returning EAX. Useful to determine whether a given basic CPUID leaf is supported before querying it.
requirements: Must be compiled and run on an x86/x86_64 target (guarded by HWY_ARCH_X86).

functions.name: hwy::x86::IsAMD
functions.description: Determines whether the current CPU vendor ID matches "AuthenticAMD" by reading CPUID leaf 0 and comparing EBX, ECX, and EDX to the AMD vendor string. Use to gate AMD-specific feature handling or workarounds.
requirements: Must be compiled and run on an x86/x86_64 target (guarded by HWY_ARCH_X86).
Meaningful result assumes CPUID instruction is available; behavior on pre-CPUID-era CPUs is undefined.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting C strings (as bytes) for use by fuzz stubs
# that call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and pass the result to APIs expecting NUL-terminated
# C strings (std::string::c_str()). We craft a variety of names/captions including
# ASCII, unicode (UTF-8), long/short, edge punctuation, repeated patterns, and
# strings resembling CPU names or profiler zone names.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

_ascii = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
_sym = " _-:/\\.,;!@#$%^&*()[]{}<>?+="
_hex = string.hexdigits.lower()

_cpu_vendors = [
    "GenuineIntel", "AuthenticAMD", "HygonGenuine", "CentaurHauls",
    "GenuineTMx86", "CyrixInstead", "TransmetaCPU", "Genuine  Intel"
]
_cpu_models = [
    "Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K", "AMD Ryzen 9 7950X", "Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6258R",
    "Apple M2", "ARM Neoverse N2", "Ampere Altra Max", "Intel(R) Atom(TM) N5105"
]
_targets = [
    "SCALAR", "SSE2", "SSSE3", "SSE4", "AVX", "AVX2", "AVX512", "NEON",
    "SVE", "SVE2", "RVV", "WASM", "PTX"
]
_zone_prefix = [
    "Init", "Compute", "Finalize", "I/O", "Decode", "Encode", "MemCopy",
    "Histogram", "Filter", "Pipeline", "ThreadPool", "Scheduler"
]

_utf8_samples = [
    "Διανύσματα", "整数演算", "спектр", "בִּנְיָן", "عناصر", "προφίλ",
    "測定", "زمان‌سنج", "프로파일", "解析", "数値", "可視化", "🔧 Profiling", "🧪 Bench"
]

_patterns = [
    lambda r: "".join(r.choice(_ascii) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 64))),
    lambda r: "".join(r.choice(_ascii + _sym) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 96))),
    lambda r: (r.choice(_zone_prefix) + ":" + r.choice(_targets)),
    lambda r: r.choice(_cpu_vendors),
    lambda r: r.choice(_cpu_models),
    lambda r: "zone_" + "".join(r.choice(_hex) for _ in range(16)),
    lambda r: "target=" + r.choice(_targets) + "; lanes=" + str(r.choice([8,16,32,64,128,256])),
    lambda r: r.choice(_utf8_samples),
    lambda r: "A" * r.randint(1, 200),  # long repeated
    lambda r: "\0".join(["part", "with", "embedded", "nuls"]) + "\0end",  # embedded NULs
]

_suffixes = ["", " (inclusive)", " [self]", " @thread0", " #1", "/core", "-fast", "_dbg"]


def _weighted_choices(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Build a list of candidate strings; include duplicates and variants to
    # increase coverage for profiler names and captions.
    res: List[str] = []
    # Deterministic mix counts based on seed randomness
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        s = r.choice(_patterns)(r)
        s += r.choice(_suffixes)
        res.append(s)
    # Add some captions including empty and whitespace-only
    res += [
        "", " ", "\t\t", "caption", "values", "array[lane]", "duration (ticks)",
        "inclusive,total", "name_with_commas,spaces", "path:C:\\tmp\\file.txt"
    ]
    # A few unicode-rich captions
    res += ["Στοιχεία", "値の一覧", "профиль", "Δt=1e-6s", "μs", "ns"]
    return res


def _compose_blob(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose 1-4 strings and join with newlines to form a single buffer from
    # which FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads. It may read slices, so ensure total size <= 4096.
    parts = _weighted_choices(r)
    r.shuffle(parts)
    take = r.randint(1, min(4, len(parts)))
    chosen = parts[:take]

    # Join with newlines, sometimes with leading/trailing whitespace
    joiner = r.choice(["\n", "\r\n", "\0", " | "])
    blob = joiner.join(chosen)

    # Occasionally prefix/suffix extra context
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        blob = (r.choice(["[ZONE] ", "CPU=", "target:", "name="]) + blob)
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        blob = blob + r.choice(["\n", "\0", " ", "\n\n"])

    b = blob.encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")

    # Ensure size cap
    if len(b) > MAX_BYTES:
        b = b[:MAX_BYTES]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Mix seed with additional randomness for variability while deterministic per seed
    r.jumpahead = getattr(r, "jumpahead", None)  # Py3.10 has no jumpahead; ignore

    # Build 1-3 concatenated chunks separated by newlines to offer variety
    chunks = []
    count = r.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(count):
        chunks.append(_compose_blob(r))
    data = b"\n".join(chunks)

    # Guarantee non-empty; include at least one short ASCII token if empty
    if not data:
        data = b"zone_default"

    # Final size clamp
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_BYTES]
    return data

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate an arbitrary binary blob used by stubs via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Goals for interesting valid inputs across provided stubs:
# - Non-empty buffer is required (many stubs bail on empty).
# - Include varying lengths to exercise modulo patterns over 64/128 bytes.
# - Include diverse byte values: ASCII, zeros, 0xFF, increasing/decreasing sequences,
#   random noise, repeating patterns, primes/step strides, and multi-byte structures
#   to form varied uint16/uint32 when combined by the stubs.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _chunk(pattern: bytes, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    if not pattern:
        return b"\x00"
    # Repeat/cycle pattern to target length
    out = (pattern * (target_len // len(pattern) + 1))[:target_len]
    return out

def _make_patterns(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pats: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Printable ASCII mix
    ascii_chars = bytes([rng.randrange(32, 127) for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 64))])
    pats.append(ascii_chars)

    # 2) All zeros
    pats.append(b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 64))

    # 3) All 0xFF
    pats.append(b"\xFF" * rng.randint(1, 64))

    # 4) Increasing byte sequence
    start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    inc_len = rng.randint(16, 128)
    pats.append(bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(inc_len)))

    # 5) Decreasing byte sequence
    start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    dec_len = rng.randint(16, 128)
    pats.append(bytes((start - i) % 256 for i in range(dec_len)))

    # 6) Repeating short motif to exercise modulo fill
    motif_len = rng.choice([1,2,3,4,5,7,8,16])
    motif = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(motif_len))
    pats.append(motif)

    # 7) Structured 16-bit little-endian values spanning range
    count16 = rng.randint(8, 64)
    vals16 = [rng.randrange(0, 0x10000) for _ in range(count16)]
    pats.append(b"".join(struct.pack('<H', v) for v in vals16))

    # 8) Structured 32-bit little-endian values spanning range
    count32 = rng.randint(4, 32)
    vals32 = [rng.randrange(0, 0x100000000) for _ in range(count32)]
    pats.append(b"".join(struct.pack('<I', v) for v in vals32))

    # 9) Alternating 0x00/0xFF pattern
    alt_len = rng.randint(32, 128)
    pats.append(bytes(0xFF if (i & 1) else 0x00 for i in range(alt_len)))

    # 10) Prime-stride sampling over 0..255 to get varied distribution
    base = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    step = rng.choice([3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23])
    plen = rng.randint(32, 128)
    pats.append(bytes((base + i*step) % 256 for i in range(plen)))

    return pats

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide overall size with bias toward small and cacheline-friendly lengths
    size_choices = [64, 128, 256, 512, 1024]
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        total_len = rng.choice(size_choices)
    else:
        total_len = rng.randint(32, min(1024, MAX_SIZE))

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Build a header that helps create varied uint16/uint32 combinations when stubs read bytes:
    # - Magic bytes, length fields, and some counters (not required by stubs, but provide structure)
    magic = b"HWYFZZ\x00"
    parts.append(magic)

    # Insert a small control block with sizes that are not used by the target directly,
    # but ensure diverse content early in the buffer.
    ctrl = struct.pack('<IIII', rng.getrandbits(32), rng.getrandbits(32), rng.randrange(1, 257), rng.randrange(0, 129))
    parts.append(ctrl)

    # Add multiple diverse patterns
    patterns = _make_patterns(rng)

    # Choose 3-6 patterns to concatenate
    rng.shuffle(patterns)
    k = rng.randint(3, 6)
    for i in range(k):
        parts.append(patterns[i])

    # Ensure we include content that exactly fills 64 and 128 bytes when cycled
    parts.append(_chunk(patterns[0], 64))
    parts.append(_chunk(patterns[1], 128))

    # Add some random noise segment
    noise_len = rng.randint(32, 192)
    parts.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(noise_len)))

    # Compose and trim/pad to desired length
    blob = b"".join(parts)
    if len(blob) < total_len:
        # Pad with a repeat of a selected pattern to hit target length exactly
        pad = _chunk(patterns[-1], total_len - len(blob))
        blob += pad
    else:
        blob = blob[:total_len]

    # Guarantee non-empty per stub requirements
    if not blob:
        blob = b"\x01"

    # Bound final size to MAX_SIZE
    return blob[:MAX_SIZE]
